title: 1919 Egyptian revolution
summary: After the First World War, Egyptians of all religions and classes rose against British occupation following the arrest and exile of Saad Zaghlul and other nationalists on 8 March 1919. Strikes, riots and rural violence were met by violent British suppression. Britain declared Egypt independent in 1922, though with limited sovereignty.

as_recorded.value: Zaghlul and others were arrested by the British on March 8 1919

where.modern_name: Egypt (Cairo, Tanta and the countryside) (proxy pin: Sultanate of Egypt, the location Wikidata lists)
where.historical_name: Egypt under British occupation and protectorate

importance.justification: A major anti-colonial uprising that forced Britain to grant limited independence and inspired other anti-colonial struggles.

audience_note: Includes violent suppression of unrest, with civilian deaths and a described campaign of terror.
